summary: Migrate legacy team-ops Slack integrations to org-bot framework and provision temporary Confluence sandbox with scoped admin group
description:
Issue summary: Migrate three legacy Slack integrations maintained by team-ops (team-ops-notify, team-ops-rotations, and onboarding-assistant) to the centralized org-bot framework. Also provision a short-lived Confluence sandbox space where the team can validate migration playbooks and delegated admin workflows before we apply changes to the main spaces.

Impact: Current integrations use older webhook tokens and per-channel app installations which are difficult to rotate and audit. This increases operational burden and creates a security risk for token leakage. The lack of a sandbox means playbooks were previously tested in production Confluence/Jira, which caused accidental page edits and permission mistakes.

Desired outcome: All three Slack apps migrated to org-bot with token rotation and centralized secrets in KMS; a Confluence sandbox (space key: TEAMOPS-SBX) created with a scoped admin group (team-ops-sandbox-admins) populated from an existing identity group. Migration runbooks and a Jira project template for sandbox testing should be created and linked into the sandbox space.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Identify legacy Slack apps: team-ops-notify, team-ops-rotations, onboarding-assistant
2) Attempt to rotate tokens — current tokens are stored in multiple places (Google Drive doc + vault) and some channels still use older webhook URLs
3) Attempt to test changes in Confluence — no isolated sandbox available, changes affect production spaces
4) Attempt to update app manifests — manual per-channel reinstall required due to legacy installs
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 Rafael: Confirmed app manifests for team-ops-notify and team-ops-rotations exist in github.com/redwood-inference/slack-apps repo. onboarding-assistant was created by an external contractor and uses legacy incoming webhooks.

2026-03-11 Security (Priya): Recommended rotating tokens before migration and using org-bot service account with restricted scopes. Suggested using org KMS for secrets and audit-enabled IAM service account.
2026-03-11 Infra (Rafael): Verified org-bot has required scopes for channels:read, chat:write, users:read. Need to add workflows for channel-level webhook replacement for contractor-created installs.
workarounds: A: Disable legacy incoming webhooks while preserving historical messages (export to archive channel and store export in S3),
B: Create temporary per-team private channel and install org-bot there for early verification before broad rollout
resolution_plan: 1) Create Confluence sandbox space TEAMOPS-SBX with space-admins set to team-ops-sandbox-admins group
2) Provision Jira sandbox project using template 'sandbox-template-v2' for playbook runs (issue key prefix SBX),
3) Migrate apps to org-bot: update manifests, perform staged reinstall, rotate tokens and store in KMS,
4) Run canary for two weeks in sandbox, capture errors and permission mismatches,
5) Roll out to production channels with scheduled maintenance window and rollback plan
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen (Requestor): Filing this to reduce manual installs and improve token rotation. Prefer sandbox approach to avoid prior incidents where test edits touched production pages.

2026-03-10 Rafael Ortiz (Assignee): I've pulled manifests and will draft migration runbook. Need confirmation on whether legal requires retention of webhook history prior to disabling. Adding security for token rotation step.

2026-03-11 Priya Nair (Security): Legal doesn't require full message retention; export summary is sufficient. We'll coordinate KMS key creation and HSM-backed rotation schedule. Will review org-bot scopes once runbook is ready.

2026-03-12 Rafael Ortiz: Provisioned Confluence space TEAMOPS-SBX (pending space key approval). Created group team-ops-sandbox-admins and added the three initial members: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz, and Anika Patel. Awaiting verification and final approval before installing org-bot in the sandbox.
2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Approved initial sandbox membership. Please include a short checklist for post-migration audits: token rotation proof, test messages, and CI job to monitor org-bot heartbeats.
